summary: Linn Fire Patrol lookout station on Horse Rock, Linn County, OR, by 1913; a 1939 cabin, removed or destroyed in the 1940s; no current site description found.

facts.status_note: Cabin removed or destroyed in the 1940s; no source describes what remains at the site

events.note: Elmer Fox in charge of the lookout station on Horse Rock (Albany Democrat, April 15, 1913, as quoted by Forest Lookouts)
New 18-mile telephone line from Holley being built to Horse Rock; earlier lookouts had walked seven miles to a phone (The Forest Log, August 1936)
William Newton, lookout on Horse Rock for twelve years, died April 28, 1940 (The Forest Log, June 1940)
Cabin removed in the 1940s per the register; firelookout.com says destroyed. Only the decade is given, so 1940 marks the start of the decade, not a known date

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register and firelookout.com date the cabin to 1939, but the 1913 report already describes a lookout station on Horse Rock. The 1939 event is the cabin, and the earlier station is recorded as a staffed event.

The 1913 report describes a telephone line already built to Horse Rock; the 1936 item describes a new line being built and recalls earlier lookouts walking seven miles to a phone. The story reports both and does not settle the question.
The register says the cabin was removed and firelookout.com says destroyed; both put it in the 1940s. The story reports both wordings.

notes_for_editor: No source describes the site today, and none confirms that the cabin site lies inside the Horse Rock Ridge research natural area. The register's 2,864 ft elevation matches the top of the area's range on Wikipedia, which suggests but does not prove a match. The 1913 and 1936 telephone accounts disagree. The Forest Log items are read through the Forest Lookouts page; the originals were not checked. Access is left unset because no source supports a level for the site. The brief has no built event, so the 1939 cabin is added.
